Author: @sashizakura9124
Content:
Heehee, Muda's cute tourist impression of Japanese People being ever so kind and nice. Try living here and working for a Japanese company as a token foreigner peon for a while. It doesn't matter how long you've lived here or how well you can speak the language - if a native decides they don't like you, you'll be stabbed in the back and whined about until you're driven away or just disposed of suddenly. Some people never even know what hit them, that's what indirect communication gets you when you're on the dark side of it. 

The moral of the story is, and it's especially true for people who work for tourist businesses here, they'll tolerate you to your face long enough to get your money. It's just hospitality. Once you're on your way, they're most likely just happy to be rid of you. Like anywhere, there are occasionally truly kind people who might go out of their way to help you find your way on the street (yes, yes, we've all heard this story) but for the most part, Japanese are no less human than other human beings worldwide. They are very capable of being petty and horrible, but societal norms mean keeping your negative feelings to yourself and working behind the scenes instead to get rid of "undesirables".  I'm glad you have had good experiences while you've visited!

Content:
1:28 Honestly as a lurker here Muta, I gotta argue with you here.

 There are great examples of respectful foreign IRL streamers in Japan such as PremierTwo, CDawgVA, and Robcdee.

PremierTwo is a perfect example— used to be English Teacher in Japan turned Streamer. He’s polite, full of energy for a man in his 40's and blends in naturally with locals, focusing on showcasing daily life and culture without disrupting anyone.
